## 2025 Abel Prize in Mathematics: Masaki Kashiwara

Masaki Kashiwara was awarded the 2025 Abel Prize for his foundational work in algebraic analysis and representation theory [en.wikipedia.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Masaki_Kashiwara) [doi.org](https://doi.org/10.1090/noti3306) [doi.org](https://doi.org/10.18257/raccefyn.3624). The Abel Prize recognizes pioneering mathematical achievements, aiming to raise the status of mathematics and foster interest among younger generations [academiceurope.com](https://www.academiceurope.com/ads_news/the-abel-prize-international-prize-of-mathematics-awarded-yearly/).

### Key Contributions and Achievements

*   **D-module Theory:**
    *   Kashiwara co-founded the analytic theory of D-modules, which utilizes sheaf-theoretic methods to study systems of linear partial differential equations (PDEs) with analytic coefficients [en.wikipedia.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Masaki_Kashiwara).
    *   His doctoral work and early research established the core foundations of D-module theory, studying differential equations using geometric and algebraic methods [en.wikipedia.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Masaki_Kashiwara) [doi.org](https://doi.org/10.18257/raccefyn.3624).
*   **Microlocal Analysis:**
    *   He pioneered concepts in microdifferential systems and the involutivity of characteristics [en.wikipedia.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Masaki_Kashiwara).
    *   His collaboration with Sato and Kawai in 1973 significantly influenced PDE analysis [en.wikipedia.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Masaki_Kashiwara).
*   **Bernstein-Sato (b-functions):**
    *   Kashiwara proved the rationality of the roots of Bernstein-Sato polynomials, using D-module theory and resolution of singularities [en.wikipedia.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Masaki_Kashiwara).
*   **Riemann-Hilbert Correspondence:**
    *   He constructed the Riemann-Hilbert correspondence, which connects D-modules with perverse sheaves and broader representation-theoretic frameworks [en.wikipedia.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Masaki_Kashiwara).
    *   This work establishes an equivalence between derived categories of D-modules (regular holonomic) and constructible sheaves, bridging topological and algebraic aspects [doi.org](https://doi.org/10.1090/noti3306) [doi.org](https://doi.org/10.18257/raccefyn.3624).
    *   This correspondence played a crucial role in proving the Kazhdan-Lusztig conjecture [doi.org](https://doi.org/10.1090/noti3306) [doi.org](https://doi.org/10.18257/raccefyn.3624).
*   **Crystal Bases and Representation Theory:**
    *   Kashiwara made influential contributions to crystal bases and crystal graphs in the context of quantum groups [en.wikipedia.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Masaki_Kashiwara) [doi.org](https://doi.org/10.1090/noti3306).
    *   His "grand loop" method provides a combinatorial description of representations as q → 0, enabling a completely combinatorial analysis [doi.org](https://doi.org/10.1090/noti3306).
*   **Connections Across Mathematics:**
    *   Kashiwara's work is recognized for its ability to connect disparate areas of mathematics, bridging analysis, geometry, and representation theory [en.wikipedia.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Masaki_Kashiwara) [doi.org](https://doi.org/10.18257/raccefyn.3624). His methods have applications in statistical physics and representation theory [doi.org](https://doi.org/10.18257/raccefyn.3624).

### Career Highlights and Recognition

*   Masaki Kashiwara is a Japanese mathematician, born in 1947 [en.wikipedia.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Masaki_Kashiwara) [doi.org](https://doi.org/10.18257/raccefyn.3624).
*   He received his BSc and MSc from the University of Tokyo and his PhD from Kyoto University, where his doctoral advisor was Mikio Sato [en.wikipedia.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Masaki_Kashiwara) [doi.org](https://doi.org/10.18257/raccefyn.3624).
*   He has held a longtime faculty position at the Research Institute for Mathematical Sciences (RIMS) at Kyoto University, also serving as its director [en.wikipedia.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Masaki_Kashiwara).
*   Kashiwara is the first Japanese national to be awarded the Abel Prize [en.wikipedia.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Masaki_Kashiwara).
*   His other recognitions include the Iyanaga Prize (1981), Asahi Prize (1988), Japan Academy Prize (1988), Kyoto Prize (2018), Chern Medal (2018), and the Order of the Sacred Treasure (2020) [en.wikipedia.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Masaki_Kashiwara).
